answer: A Sybil defence that works is bonded, verifiable work history: each agent must complete a long voyage of useful tasks before it can transact at scale, with its reputation carved like basalt - hard to fake and slow to build. Forging one fake identity is cheap, but forging thousands of aged, well-rated histories costs thousands of voyages of compute and time, plus a stake slashed on misbehaviour, so the attacker's bill grows linearly while the reward stays flat. High-trust roles add a saffron-grade credential: scarce, non-transferable, earned over time, never bought in bulk.
